'''David Allan Butterfield''' (born January 14, 1946) is an American biological chemist. During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Butterfield was named among the world's leading [[Alzheimer's disease]] experts by Expertscape, an online base of biomedical expertise.  He is a Fellow of the Society for Free Radical Biology and Medicine.

==Early life and education==
Butterfield was born on January 14, 1946<ref name="CV">{{cite web |title=D. ALLAN BUTTERFIELD CV |url=https://pa.as.uky.edu/sites/default/files/cv/Vitae_with_Supplemental_Vitae%20%203-12-20%20%28Repaired%29.pdf |website=pa.as.uky.edu |access-date=April 20, 2021 |archive-date=April 22, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210422012358/https://pa.as.uky.edu/sites/default/files/cv/Vitae_with_Supplemental_Vitae%20%203-12-20%20(Repaired).pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> to father Francis Butterfield in [[Brownville, Maine]].<ref name="marriage">{{cite news |title=MRS DAVID ALLAN BUTTERFIELD |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/76160078/marriage-of-tuthill-butterfield/ |access-date=April 20, 2021 |publisher=The Bangor Daily News |date=June 12, 1968 |location=Bangor, Maine|via=newspapers.com}}</ref> He attended Brownville Junction High School where he was elected president of the Future Teachers of America Club as a senior.<ref>{{cite news |title=New President |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/76161129/new-president/ |access-date=April 20, 2021 |publisher=The Bangor Daily News |date=April 1, 1964}}</ref>

Butterfield graduated from the [[University of Maine]] in 1968 as a member of the [[Phi Beta Kappa]], [[Phi Kappa Phi]] honor society, and the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref name="marriage"/> Following this, he enrolled at [[Duke University]] for his PhD and became an [[National Institutes of Health]] (NIH) Postdoctoral Fellow in Neuroscience from [[Duke University School of Medicine]].<ref name="UK bio">{{cite web |title=D. Allan Butterfield |url=https://chem.as.uky.edu/users/dabcns |website=chem.as.uky.edu |access-date=April 20, 2021}}</ref> Upon graduating, Butterfield and his wife Maria left for [[Rhodesia]] on a teaching assignment.<ref name="marriage"/> He taught all of the secondary school mathematics classes in Murewa while his wife Marcia taught six classes of English and was in charge of the library.<ref>{{cite news |title=Two U-M Graduates Serve As Teachers in Rhodesia |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/76160478/two-u-m-graduates-serve-as-teachers-in/ |access-date=April 20, 2021 |publisher=The Bangor Daily News |date=April 1, 1969|via=newspapers.com}}</ref> Upon returning from their mission, Butterfield was hospitalized for hepatitis.<ref>{{cite news |title=Missionaries Unable To Be At Orono Church |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/76160988/missionaries-unable-to-be-at-orono/ |access-date=April 20, 2021 |publisher=The Bangor Daily News |date=July 9, 1971|via=newspapers.com}}</ref>

==Career==
Butterfield accepted a faculty position at the [[University of Kentucky]] (UK) in 1975.<ref name="Feldman">{{cite news |last1=Feldman |first1=Jacinta |title=White House honors UK chemist |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/76159804/white-house-honors-uk-chemist/ |access-date=April 20, 2021 |publisher=Lexington Herald-Leader |date=September 22, 1998|via=newspapers.com}}</ref> He continued his research on [[dystrophy]] from Duke as an [[assistant professor]] of chemistry. In his laboratory, his research on  muscular dystrophy indicated to him that the disease is one that affects all the cells of the body.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Runyon |first1=Keith |title=New theory on muscular dystrophy is studied |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/76160063/new-theory-on-muscular-dystrophy-is/ |access-date=April 20, 2021 |publisher=The Courier-Journal |date=March 14, 1976|via=newspapers.com}}</ref> In 1986, Butterfield was named director of the University of Kentucky Research Center for Membrane Sciences.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mead |first1=Andy |title=Kentucky professors address the mysteries of membranes |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/76160050/kentucky-professors-address-the/ |access-date=April 20, 2021 |publisher=Lexington Herald-Leader |date=October 13, 1986|via=newspapers.com}}</ref> His research and teaching was recognized by the [[White House]] in 1998 with the Presidential Award for Science Mathematics and Engineering Mentoring.<ref name="Feldman"/>

At the turn of the 21st century, Butterfield found evidence suggesting that [[vitamin E]] could help prevent Alzheimer's disease. His research, funded by the [[National Institutes of Health]] (NIH), came to this conclusion by comparing [[amyloid beta]] peptide in an animal model to the same compound in humans.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Elliott |first1=Allison |title=Researcher Uncovers Clues to Alzheimer's |url=http://www.uky.edu/PR/News/Archives/2004/Nov2004/041104_butterfield_finding.htm |website=uky.edu |access-date=April 21, 2021 |date=November 4, 2004}}</ref> Later, he was appointed chair of the Neural Oxidative Metabolism and Death Study Section of the [[Center for Scientific Review]] (CSR) of the NIH.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chemistry Professor Allan Butterfield Awarded NIH Chair |url=https://chem.as.uky.edu/chemistry-professor-allan-butterfield-awarded-nih-chair-0 |website=chem.as.uky.edu |access-date=April 21, 2021 |date=March 29, 2011}}</ref> In 2012, Butterfield was named a UK Alumni Association Endowed Professor of Biological Chemistry<ref>{{cite web |title=Allan Butterfield: UK Alumni Association Endowed Professor of Biological Chemistry |url=https://www.as.uky.edu/podcasts/allan-butterfield-uk-alumni-association-endowed-professor-biological-chemistry-uk-half-carl |website=as.uky.ed |access-date=April 21, 2021 |date=January 24, 2012}}</ref> and was elected a Fellow of the Society for Free Radical Biology and Medicine.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Springs |first1=Guy |title=Allan Butterfield Named Prestigious SFRBM Fellow |url=https://chem.as.uky.edu/allan-butterfield-named-prestigious-sfrbm-fellow |website=chem.as.uky.edu |access-date=April 21, 2021 |date=November 20, 2012}}</ref> As a result of his research into Alzheimer's disease, Butterfield was also the recipient of the society's Mentoring Excellence Award<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fawns |first1=Will |title=Butterfield to Receive Mentoring Excellence Award from Major National Society |url=https://chem.as.uky.edu/butterfield-receive-mentoring-excellence-award-major-national-society |website=chem.as.uky.edu |access-date=April 21, 2021 |date=October 16, 2014}}</ref> and 2013 Discovery Award.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Perry |first1=Allison |title=UK Researcher Allan Butterfield Earns 2013 Discovery Award |url=https://chem.as.uky.edu/uk-researcher-allan-butterfield-earns-2013-discovery-award |website=chem.as.uky.edu |access-date=April 21, 2021 |date=July 22, 2013}}</ref>

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Butterfield was named among the world's leading Alzheimer's disease experts by Expertscape, an online base of biomedical expertise. He is among the top 0.007% of scholars worldwide based on authorship of Alzheimer's-related publications indexed in the [[PubMed]] database and ranked tenth out of nearly 150,000 scholars worldwide and sixth in the United States.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Chapin |first1=Elizabeth |title=Butterfield Recognized as a Leading Alzheimer's Expert |url=https://uknow.uky.edu/research/butterfield-recognized-leading-alzheimer-s-expert |website=uknow.uky.edu |access-date=April 20, 2021 |date=October 9, 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Butterfield met his wife Maria while attending the University of Maine on November 6, 1965. They married upon graduating in 1968 and have one daughter together. Prior to her retirement, Maria worked as a nurse.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Grimes |first1=Le Datta |title=Working for the 'hidden' patients |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/76159788/working-for-the-hidden-patients/ |access-date=April 20, 2021 |publisher=Lexington Herald-Leader |date=January 21, 1999|via=newspapers.com}}</ref>
